newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to raise $2 bln in fx bonds by start of '97.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to raise $2 bln in fx bonds by start of '97.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday Turkey would raise $2 billion through issuing foreign currency-denominated bonds by the end of this year.

"In the first auction $1.2 billion entered into Turkey from the accounts of Turkish banks abroad. There is another $2 billion more which will come by the beginning of next year," Ciller told her party's parliamentary group meeting.

Last month, the Turkish treasury sold $1.12 billion worth of three-year foreign currency denominated bonds to Turkish banks at an interest rate of LIBOR plus 260 basis points. The bonds had a put option at the end of the second year.
Ciller said the government aimed to extend short domestic borrowing maturites by issuing foreign currency bonds.
"Our average (domestic) borrowing maturity is 4.5 months. It is seven years in the European Union. Our problem is not the level of debt stocks but its short maturity structure," Ciller said.
